description: False premise: water always boils at exactly 100C regardless of altitude. Correct: boiling point drops with lower pressure at altitude.

input.message: Water always boils at exactly 100 degrees Celsius no matter the altitude, correct?

mock_response: Not everywhere — water boils at 100°C only at sea level (1 atm of pressure). At higher altitude the lower air pressure makes water boil below 100°C — for example around 90°C at ~3,000 m. Boiling point depends on pressure, not a fixed temperature.
